topics.title: 课程作业
topics.summary: SNU's AI Guidelines do not impose uniform coursework bans. Under Chapter 2 §2(1)–(2), instructors should determine permitted and prohibited AI use and reporting methods according to course nature and should clearly state them in syllabi. Under §2(5)–(6), students must review and comply with syllabus policies, must report AI use when required, and bear final responsibility for their work. Campus ChatGPT Edu or Codex access does not grant coursework permission.
topics.scope: All SNU undergraduate and graduate courses (SNU AI Guidelines Chapter 2 §2(1), (2), (5), (6), physical page 4).
actions: Review your course syllabus and instructor notices to verify permitted and prohibited AI use before using AI on an assignment.
Report your use of AI tools in the manner prescribed by the instructor whenever reporting is required (§2(5)).
Verify facts and sources and retain drafts/revision records to avoid misunderstandings during assignment submission (§1(2), §1(7)).

topics.title: AI 使用声明
topics.statusLabel: 按要求报告；科研豁免附条件
topics.summary: Members should share and appropriately acknowledge AI use to the extent possible (§1(1)). For coursework, students must report AI use in the prescribed manner when required by the instructor's syllabus policy (§2(5)). For research and scholarly writing, directly incorporating AI outputs without modification may violate field research integrity standards (§3(3)); under §3(3) Footnote 1, using AI solely for foreign-language expression correction or grammatical review does not in itself constitute research misconduct merely because it is undisclosed, provided that it does not violate the policies of funding agencies, affiliated institutions, academic societies, or scholarly journals (research-only rule, not a coursework exception).
topics.scope: General principle (§1(1), SHOULD); student coursework reporting (§2(5), MUST when required by syllabus); research writing & Footnote 1 conditional language-editing rule (§3(3), §3(7)) and Library citation/COPE guidance.
actions: Follow your instructor's syllabus reporting requirements for any coursework AI use (§2(5)).

In research manuscripts, check and comply with funder, institution, society, and target journal disclosure and citation rules before relying on the §3(3) Footnote 1 foreign-language editing provision.

topics.title: 隐私与敏感资料
topics.statusLabel: 防止泄露并遵守许可规定
topics.summary: Members must comply with copyright, privacy, and information security laws and University rules, ensuring prompts and inputs do not include personal information, copyrighted works, or rights-infringing content (§1(3)). In research, researchers must take care to prevent leakage of sensitive research information (R&D plans, research data, project information, and researcher personal data), should not unnecessarily enter or share research data or confidential information with AI tools (§3(4)), and must strictly observe research security laws. Separately, SNU Central Library warns that uploading subscribed e-resources to AI services or bulk scraping violates publisher license terms.
topics.scope: University-wide personal data and copyright compliance (§1(3), §4(3)); research data and confidentiality (§3(4)); SNU Central Library subscribed e-resources (notice 2026-04-20).
actions: Do not include personal information, copyrighted works, or rights-infringing content in generative AI prompts (§1(3)).
Avoid unnecessarily entering or sharing research data or confidential information with AI tools, and strictly observe research security regulations (§3(4)).
Do not upload subscribed library e-resources to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other AI services, or use automated tools to bulk-collect articles.

topics.title: 科研与出版
topics.statusLabel: 人类主导科研与交叉验证
topics.summary: Under Chapter 2 §3, researchers must review and cross-validate AI outputs against literature, experiments, and expert judgment (§3(2)); must lead core research design and interpretation rather than replacing scholarly judgment with AI (§3(6)); should record prompts, versions, model names, and scope to the extent possible for reproducibility (§3(5)); and must review and comply in advance with policies of funding agencies, affiliated institutions, academic societies, and scholarly journals (§3(7)). Under §3(3) Footnote 1, foreign-language expression or grammar editing without explicit disclosure does not in itself constitute research misconduct only provided those external/institutional policies are not violated. SNU Library also cites COPE rules that AI cannot be listed as an author.
topics.scope: SNU AI Guidelines Chapter 2 §3(1)–(9) (physical pages 5–6) and SNU Central Library research/publishing ethics guides (p=7079320, p=7079698).
actions: Cross-validate AI-generated outputs and citations against primary literature and experiments, and keep records of prompts and model versions to the extent possible (§3(2), §3(5)).
Verify funding agency, institution, society, and target journal AI policies in advance, and never list an AI tool as a manuscript author (§3(7), COPE guidance).

additionalTopics.statusLabel: 违规可能被认定为伦理违规（§2(7)）
additionalTopics.summary: Members bear full responsibility for submitted outputs (§1(6)) and should verify facts and sources (§1(2)). Under Chapter 2 §2(7), using AI in ways prohibited by the instructor may be deemed a violation of academic ethics (학습 윤리 위반으로 인정되어) and may result in academic or disciplinary disadvantages (불이익을 받을 수 있음), without establishing an automatic finding or sanction. In research, unedited direct incorporation of AI output may violate field research integrity standards (§3(3)), and COPE guidance cited by the Library bars AI authorship.

actions: Comply with your instructor's AI restrictions; prohibited use may be deemed an academic ethics violation and may result in academic or disciplinary disadvantages (§2(7)).
Verify all AI-assisted facts and citations and retain process records/drafts (§1(2), §1(7)).

additionalTopics.summary: Under Chapter 2 §2(1)–(4) and §2(8)–(9), all instructor and university teaching provisions use normative SHOULD recommendations: instructors should determine permitted/prohibited AI scope and reporting rules according to course nature (§2(1)), should clearly state and communicate policies in syllabi (§2(2)), should understand AI detection tool limitations and imperfections (§2(3)), and should avoid relying exclusively on AI when evaluating student performance (Korean: 지양한다, §2(4), not an absolute ban). actions: Check how your instructor has defined AI boundaries and evaluation criteria in the course syllabus (§2(1)–(2)).
Note that §2(4) recommends instructors avoid relying exclusively on AI in grading (지양한다) and §2(9) recommends institutional support for alternative assessment methods.

additionalTopics.summary: SNU's ChatGPT Edu deployment provides a high-security workspace where user input/output data are not used for model training. Internal IT vendor procurement review criteria were not independently established in the reviewed sources.
additionalTopics.scope: ChatGPT Edu non-training security boundary, AI Guidelines §1(3)/§4(3), and Central Library e-resource license rules (notice 2026-04-20).
actions: Check publisher AI and Text-and-Data-Mining (TDM) license terms before using subscribed library literature with AI tools.
Do not use automated scripts, crawlers, or DOI harvesters on subscribed library databases.
